title: Absolute linear-form expectation near Gaussian value
statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that for every dimension $n$, every coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb R^n$ with $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, and every real $\varepsilon$ satisfying $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for all $i$, the expected absolute value of the corresponding linear form on a uniformly random Boolean-cube point differs from $\sqrt{2/\pi}$ by at most $C\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: There exists a positive real constant $C$.
Every coefficient satisfies $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for some real $\varepsilon$.
